question: Should Slack Events API delivery reject private and non-global callback targets by default, apart from the explicit loopback test allowance?
rationale: The hardening is a sound SSRF and DNS-rebinding defense, but it intentionally makes some previously accepted private-network callback configurations fail, so repository policy cannot determine the compatibility boundary alone.

options.title: Adopt strict default
options.body: Accept the private-target compatibility break as the intended Slack provider security boundary and document the resulting callback requirements.

options.title: Make strictness opt-in
options.body: Preserve existing target acceptance by default and expose the hardened restriction through an explicit server setting with tests for both modes.

options.title: Pause pending policy
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers decide whether private-network Slack-compatible receivers are a supported Crabline use case.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict default
recommendation.body: Accept the private-target compatibility break as the intended Slack provider security boundary and document the resulting callback requirements.
